items.action: Patch NetScaler ADC/Gateway to 14.1-73.37 / 13.1-64.23 (or FIPS/NDcPP equivalents) immediately. If you cannot patch today, isolate the admin interface and hunt for post-exploitation artifacts.
items.details: CISA has added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue with a fix deadline of September 30, and UK NCSC plus Dutch agencies issued alerts of their own.
items.summary: Two remote zero-days in NetScaler ADC and Gateway are under rapid global exploitation: CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated command execution via improper input validation) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory overflow enabling DoS or RCE).
items.title: Citrix NetScaler zero-days under active exploitation

items.action: Upgrade GitLab, audit the endpoint's access logs for encoded path tricks, and restrict instance exposure.
items.details: The route %63ommits bypasses GitLab Workhorse route handling while Rails still processes the request. Leaked secrets like gitlab-secrets.json and database.yml can snowball into full instance compromise.
items.summary: CVE-2026-85706 (CVSS 10.0) lets an unauthenticated attacker read arbitrary files from a GitLab server: the body-upload helper processes file.path on POST /api/v4/projects/:id/repository/commits before authentication.
items.title: GitLab unauthenticated file-read flaw scores CVSS 10.0

items.action: Update on-premises servers to 2025.11.7 or 2026.1.3, or install the security patch plugin (works back to 2017.1). TeamCity Cloud is already mitigated.
items.details: Compromising the CI/CD server endangers build artifacts and the whole software supply chain downstream.
items.summary: CVE-2026-63077 is an authentication-bypass in TeamCity On-Premises agent-polling protocol handling that yields remote code execution with the server process's OS privileges.
items.title: JetBrains TeamCity On-Premises: RCE without credentials

items.action: Install Oracle's June 10 patch on every PeopleSoft instance; firewall-rule workarounds alone no longer stop the attack.
items.details: Organizations that patched are protected; those relying on the firewall rule should hunt for web shells planted via the PSEMHUB endpoint.
items.summary: Mandiant reports (Sep 25) that ShinyHunters bypassed the recommended firewall-rule mitigation for the Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day with a single-character request substitution. Dozens of systems worldwide now have web shells.
items.title: PeopleSoft zero-day: firewall workarounds defeated

items.details: Reuters reporting matched sample data to real people; the group says it is not seeking ransom but wants correction of a May FBI advisory about its extortion methods. The jobs portals remain offline.
items.summary: The FBI told staff it has declared a 'cyber security incident' after ShinyHunters exploited an Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability in the FBIJobs.gov portal, exposing agents' names, home addresses, SSNs, job titles and some medical records. The group claims 2-3 TB of personnel data.
items.title: FBI confirms 'cyber security incident' after ShinyHunters breach

items.details: Taiwan-based Advantech is a major industrial PC/IoT manufacturer. Chaos claims the company is ignoring the situation; Advantech has not publicly responded.
items.summary: Ransomware group Chaos claims to have compromised advantech.com and is publishing 5% of the stolen data because management 'has not contacted them' — giving the company 48 hours before a full dump.
items.title: Advantech hit by Chaos ransomware; 48-hour ultimatum

items.details: Leak-site listings mark disclosure dates, which may differ from the actual compromise dates.
items.summary: Braincipher, one of the most active ransomware operations of 2026, added two US victims to its dark-web leak site on September 29: healthcare provider northeastrehab.com and logistics firm trailerbridge.com.
items.title: Braincipher claims two new US victims

items.details: Apple is investigating alongside Tata; the leak cuts at the trust underpinning Apple's India manufacturing bet, which is on track to make 26% of the world's iPhones in 2026.
items.summary: Leaked files from Tata Electronics expose Apple's iPhone 18 Pro supply chain — component lists, supplier mappings, and drop-test photos carrying Apple's 'confidential' watermarks. Tata has restricted internal access to sensitive systems and hired a global consultant for a forensic audit.
items.title: Tata Electronics breach leaks iPhone 18 Pro supply-chain data

items.details: Globally, 1,034 organizations were publicly named as ransomware victims in August — the highest monthly total of 2026. Manufacturing, professional services, and IT/ITES were the hardest-hit sectors.
items.summary: Ransomware activity climbed to its highest monthly level of 2026 in August, and India was the most targeted country in Asia-Pacific with 24 claimed victims, ranking seventh worldwide, per Cyble Research and Intelligence Labs (CRIL).
items.title: Ransomware hits 2026 high; India most targeted in APAC

items.details: DailyDarkWeb reported the listing on September 29. No samples have been independently authenticated, and there is no public confirmation from the company — treat this as an allegation to monitor, not an established breach.
items.summary: An underground listing alleges approximately 116 GB of documents belonging to United Group India (united-group.in) are for sale. The claim is unverified and no compromise has been confirmed.
items.title: Alleged 116 GB leak targets United Group India (unverified)
